The Chinese city of Ningxia had fallen while the Manchu city still held out; Du Xing'a was recalled to court, made General of Xi'an, put in charge of Gansu operations, and appointed acting governor-general of Shaanxi and Gansu.
漢城 is the Chinese city and 滿城 the Manchu city, not a quarter and a banner city.

Raiders from Yanchi and Guyuan held Yuan Town in Anhua and threatened the grain route at Ningtiaoliang; Du Xing'a posted detachments at Huamachi, Dingbian, and Ningtiaoliang, while rebels south of Jingyuan burned forts, seized the dams, and prepared to breach the canal to flood the government camps; he shifted his headquarters to the southeast of the city.

Raiders from Yanchi and Guyuan held Yuan Town in Anhua and threatened the grain route at Ningtiaoliang; Du Xing'a posted detachments at Huamachi, Dingbian, and Ningtiaoliang, while rebels south of Jingyuan burned forts, seized the dams, repaired the weirs, and prepared to breach the canal to flood the government camps; he shifted his headquarters to the southeast of the city.
修堰, repairing the weirs, is omitted from the idiomatic English.
The bandit strength at Ningxia gradually tightened; with specious words they begged for pacification to gain time, while secretly breaching the West River to flood the government army.
The bandits at Ningxia were gradually hard-pressed; with specious words they begged for pacification to gain time, while secretly breaching the West River to flood the government army.
賊勢漸蹙 means the rebels were increasingly hard-pressed, not that their strength tightened.

Du Xing'a rejected their surrender and redoubled preparations; he relieved the banner city, took the eastern stockades, routed them at Ximen Bridge, sent detachments to clear Dashuikeng and Wuzhongbao, beheaded the Muslim leader Ma Youfu, and the army's prestige rose sharply.

Du Xing'a rejected their surrender and redoubled preparations; he relieved the Manchu city, took the eastern stockades, routed them at Ximen Bridge, sent detachments to clear Dashuikeng and Wuzhongbao, beheaded the Muslim leader Ma Youfu, and the army's prestige rose sharply.
滿城 is the Manchu city, not a banner city.

He was summoned to Beijing to command the Shenji Camp, made Imperial Commissioner, and given four armies under Vice Commandant-General Chunshou and Admirals Zhang Yao, Song Qing, and Bodyguard Chen Guorui; in seniority he ranked above Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang.

He was summoned to Beijing to command the Shenji Camp, made Imperial Commissioner, and given four armies under Vice Commandant-General Chunshou and Provincial Military Commanders Zhang Yao and Song Qing, and Bodyguard Chen Guorui; his name was listed above Li Hongzhang and Zuo Zongtang.
提督 is provincial military commander, not admiral; 列名在上 means his name was listed above theirs, not that the text states seniority.

An edict summoned Du Xing'a to the capital to administer the Shenji Camp, granted him the title of Imperial Commissioner, and placed under him the four armies of Vice Commandant-General Chunshou, Admirals Zhang Yao and Song Qing, and Bodyguard Chen Guorui; his name was listed above Hongzhang and Zongtang.

An edict summoned Du Xing'a to the capital to administer the Shenji Camp, granted him the title of Imperial Commissioner, and placed under him the four armies of Vice Commandant-General Chunshou, Provincial Military Commanders Zhang Yao and Song Qing, and Bodyguard Chen Guorui; his name was listed above Hongzhang and Zongtang.
提督 is provincial military commander, not admiral.
Under Daoguang he followed General Yijing to Zhejiang, rose to first-class bodyguard, and was eventually promoted to Chahar commandant-general.
Under Daoguang he followed the Yangwei General Yijing to Zhejiang, rose to first-class bodyguard, and was eventually promoted to Chahar commandant-general.
揚威將軍, the Yangwei General, is omitted.

With Sengge Rinchen he stormed the outer camps repeatedly; the rebels withdrew to Dongguang and Lianzhen and fought for months with Xi Ling'a often in the van; in the first month of the fifth year the place fell and Lin Fengxiang was captured; he received the hereditary rank of Second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and the title Yijing Batuer.

With Sengge Rinchen he stormed the outer camps repeatedly; the rebels withdrew to Dongguang and Lianzhen and fought for months with Xi Ling'a often in the van; in the first month of the fifth year the place fell and Lin Fengxiang was captured; he received the hereditary rank of Second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and the title Yijing'a Baturu.
伊精阿巴圖魯 is Yijing'a Baturu; the English drops 阿.

Following Sengge Rinchen he repeatedly stormed the bandit camps outside the city; the bandits fled to hold Dongguang and Lianzhen; fighting went on for several months; Xi Ling'a was often the army's spearhead; in the first month of the fifth year it was captured; the bandit leader Lin Fengxiang was taken; he was granted the hereditary office of Second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and the epithet Yijing Batuer.

Following Sengge Rinchen he repeatedly stormed the bandit camps outside the city; the bandits fled to hold Dongguang and Lianzhen; fighting went on for several months; Xi Ling'a was often the army's spearhead; in the first month of the fifth year it was captured; the bandit leader Lin Fengxiang was taken; he was granted the hereditary office of Second-class Commandant of Light Chariots and the epithet Yijing'a Baturu.
伊精阿巴圖魯 is Yijing'a Baturu; the English drops 阿.
On first reaching Suizhou he met defeat; his brother Du Xing'a was sent to help; he was soon dismissed and Guan Wen took command.
On first reaching Suizhou he met defeat; his elder brother Du Xing'a was sent to help; he was soon dismissed and Guan Wen took command.
兄 is elder brother, not brother unspecified.
He followed in recovering De'an prefectural city, had his original office restored, and was originally stationed to secure the northern defense.
He followed in recovering De'an prefectural city, had his original office restored, and was stationed to secure the northern defense.
原駐 here means he was stationed to hold the north, parallel to 復原官; 'originally' misreads 原.
Fu Xing, of the Murca clan, served as a Manchu bannerman of the Plain White Banner and was a great-grandson of Commandant-General Mukedengbu.
Fu Xing, of the Murca clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner and was a great-grandson of Commandant-General Mukedengbu.
滿洲正白旗人 is banner identity, not an office he served as.
In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to brigadier-general of the Gaozhou garrison in Guangdong.
In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to regional commander of the Gaozhou garrison in Guangdong.
總兵 is a regional commander, not a brigadier-general.
In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to brigadier-general of Gaozhou Garrison in Guangdong.
In the first year of Xianfeng he was promoted to regional commander of Gaozhou Garrison in Guangdong.
總兵 is a regional commander, not a brigadier-general.
In the second year he suppressed the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba and bandits in Yulin and Bobai, received the title Gang'an Batuer, and was made provincial admiral of Guangxi.
In the second year he suppressed the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba and bandits in Yulin and Bobai, received the title Gang'an Baturu, and was made provincial military commander of Guangxi.
提督 is a provincial military commander, not an admiral; 巴圖魯 is baturu.
In the second year he pacified the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba and the local bandits of Yulin and Bobai, was granted the epithet Gang'an Batuer, and was promoted to provincial admiral of Guangxi.

In the second year he pacified the Luojing bandit Ling Shiba and the local bandits of Yulin and Bobai, was granted the epithet Gang'an Baturu, and was promoted to provincial military commander of Guangxi.
提督 is a provincial military commander, not an admiral; 巴圖魯 is baturu.

With Admiral Deng Shaoliang he took Dongba, recovered Gaochun, helped capture Taiping, returned to Nanjing, and fought repeatedly at Gaoqiaomen, Shangfang Bridge, Tongji Gate, and Yuhuatai; he rose to second-rank insignia and became acting General of Jiangning.

With Provincial Military Commander Deng Shaoliang he took Dongba, recovered Gaochun, helped capture Taiping, returned to Nanjing, and fought repeatedly at Gaoqiaomen, Shangfang Bridge, Tongji Gate, and Yuhuatai; he rose to second-rank insignia and became acting General of Jiangning.
提督 is a provincial military commander, not an admiral.

Together with Admiral Deng Shaoliang he defeated the bandits at Dongba, recovered Gaochun, joined in capturing Taiping, returned the army to Jiangning, and repeatedly attacked the bandits at Gaoqiaomen, Shangfang Bridge, Tongji Gate, and Yuhuatai; he was promoted to second-rank hat ornament and made acting General of Jiangning.

Together with Provincial Military Commander Deng Shaoliang he defeated the bandits at Dongba, recovered Gaochun, joined in capturing Taiping, returned the army to Jiangning, and repeatedly attacked the bandits at Gaoqiaomen, Shangfang Bridge, Tongji Gate, and Yuhuatai; he was promoted to second-rank hat ornament and made acting General of Jiangning.
提督 is a provincial military commander, not an admiral.
On his mother's death he was recalled from mourning to stay with the army.
On his mother's death he was kept with the army instead of leaving to mourn.
奪情留軍 means mourning was curtailed so he would stay with the army, not that he was recalled after leaving.
Hearing that Fu Xing and Guoliang were at odds, the court had Yiliang investigate and then sent Fu Xing to Jiangxi to join operations there.
Hearing that Fu Xing and Guoliang were at odds, the emperor had Yiliang investigate and then sent Fu Xing to Jiangxi to join operations there.
上 is the emperor, as the literal English says; 'the court' drops it.
After Chonghuan's line died out the family settled at Runing; a son Wenbi won merit in service and was enrolled in the Ningguta Han banners.
After a descendant of Chonghuan died, the family lodged at Runing; there was a son, Wenbi won merit in service and was enrolled in the Ningguta Han banners.
裔死 is one descendant's death. 'The line died out' contradicts 有子文弼, and 流寓 is lodging away from home, not simply settling.
Five generations later came Fuming'a, who served as armored cavalry in the Kashgar campaign, became commandant of valiant cavalry, and rose to company commander.
Five generations later came Fuming'a, who served as armored cavalry in the Kashgar campaign, became a lieutenant of valiant cavalry, and rose to regimental commander.
驍騎校 is a lieutenant, not a commandant; 參領 is a regimental commander, not a company commander.

After five generations Fuming'a came forth; as an armored cavalryman he followed the campaign in Kashgar, was appointed commandant of valiant cavalry, and was repeatedly promoted to company commander.

After five generations Fuming'a came forth; as an armored cavalryman he followed the campaign in Kashgar, was appointed lieutenant of valiant cavalry, and was repeatedly promoted to regimental commander.
驍騎校 is a lieutenant, not a commandant; 參領 is a regimental commander, not a company commander.

In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Qishan at Yangzhou, was shot at Dongqingpu, bound his wound and kept fighting, killed dozens, was promoted to deputy company commander, and received a jade horn cup as a special gift.

In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Qishan at Yangzhou, was shot at Dongqingpu, bound his wound and kept fighting, killed dozens, was promoted to regimental colonel, and received a jade archer's thumb-ring as a special gift.
協領 is a banner regimental colonel, not a deputy company commander; 玉《角枼》 is a broken 玉韘, an archer's thumb-ring, not a horn cup.

In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Imperial Commissioner Qishan's army at Yangzhou, fought at Dongqingpu, received a gunshot wound, bound his wound and fought fiercely, killed and decapitated several tens, was promoted to deputy company commander, and was specially granted a jade horn cup.

In the third year of Xianfeng he followed Imperial Commissioner Qishan's army at Yangzhou, fought at Dongqingpu, received a gunshot wound, bound his wound and fought fiercely, killed and decapitated several tens, was promoted to regimental colonel, and was specially granted a jade archer's thumb-ring.
協領 is a banner regimental colonel, not a deputy company commander; 玉《角枼》 is a broken 玉韘, an archer's thumb-ring, not a horn cup.

In the fifth year at Hong Bridge he ordered his men to hold fire until twenty paces, killed the rebel leader, swept both flanks for ambushers, routed the enemy, and received the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.

In the fifth year at Hongqiao he ordered his men to loose their arrows only within twenty paces, killed the rebel leader, swept both flanks for ambushers, routed the enemy, and received the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.
虹橋 is Hongqiao; 發矢 is loosing arrows, not holding firearm fire.

In the fifth year he fought at Hong Bridge, ordered his troops not to shoot until within twenty paces of the bandits, shot dead the bandit chieftain, divided into two wings to search out ambushing bandits, the bandits collapsed and fled, and he was given the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.

In the fifth year he fought at Hongqiao, ordered his troops not to shoot until within twenty paces of the bandits, shot dead the bandit chieftain, divided into two wings to search out ambushing bandits, the bandits collapsed and fled, and he was given the nominal rank of vice commandant-general.
虹橋 is Hongqiao, not Hong Bridge.

In the ninth year Dexing'a was dismissed for misconduct and the northern army lacked a commander; troops reverted to He Chun's control until He Chun recommended Fuming'a as a man fit to hold an independent command, and the court ordered him to assist He Chun.

In the ninth year Dexing'a was dismissed for misconduct and the northern army lacked a commander; troops reverted to Hechun's control until Hechun recommended Fuming'a as a man fit to hold an independent command, and the court ordered him to assist Hechun.
和春 is a single name, not a surname He plus Chun.

In the ninth year Dexing'a was dismissed for misconduct; the northern army had no appointed commander-in-chief; troops were ordered to return to He Chun's control; another brave and resourceful man fit to hold an independent command was to be chosen; He Chun recommended Fuming'a; an edict ordered him to assist in He Chun's military affairs.

In the ninth year Dexing'a was dismissed for misconduct; the northern army had no appointed commander-in-chief; troops were ordered to return to Hechun's control; another brave and resourceful man fit to hold an independent command was to be chosen; Hechun recommended Fuming'a; an edict ordered him to assist in Hechun's military affairs.
和春 is a single name, not a surname He plus Chun.
Fuming'a took twelve wounds; the court let him vacate his post and return to his banner for treatment; crippled by his injuries, he retired at full pay on his former rank.
Fuming'a took twelve wounds; an edict let him vacate his post and return to his banner for treatment; crippled by his injuries, he retired at full pay on his former rank.
詔 is an edict, which the literal English keeps and the idiomatic drops.

That autumn he led elite troops to Linhuai, joined Sengge Rinchen against Miao Peilin, was made assistant commander, and through Zhan Qilun, Kemonge, and Chen Guorui won successive victories until Peilin was killed.

That autumn he led elite troops to Linhuai, joined Sengge Rinchen against Miao Peilin, was made assistant commander, and through Zhan Qilun, Kemeng'e, and Chen Guorui won successive victories until Peilin was executed.
克蒙額 is Kemeng'e; 伏誅 is execution, not merely being killed.

That autumn he personally led picked troops to relieve Linhuai, joined Sengge Rinchen in suppressing Miao Peilin, was ordered to assist in military affairs, and directed his subordinates Zhan Qilun, Kemonge, Chen Guorui, and others to advance; they repeatedly defeated the bandits and Peilin was executed in hiding.

That autumn he personally led picked troops to relieve Linhuai, joined Sengge Rinchen in suppressing Miao Peilin, was ordered to assist in military affairs, and directed his subordinates Zhan Qilun, Kemeng'e, Chen Guorui, and others to advance; they repeatedly defeated the bandits and Peilin was executed.
伏誅 does not mean he was executed in hiding; 克蒙額 is Kemeng'e.
The foreign red-banner fleet was then disbanded and sent back to Guangdong under Admiral Wu Quanmei, and several thousand infantry were cut.
The red-receipt boats were then disbanded and sent back to Guangdong under Provincial Military Commander Wu Quanmei, and several thousand infantry were cut.
紅單船 are red-receipt junks, not a foreign fleet; 提督 is a provincial military commander.
Thereupon the red-banner foreign ships were disbanded and Admiral Wu Quanmei led them back to Guangdong; several thousand infantry were judiciously reduced.
Thereupon the red-receipt boats were disbanded and Provincial Military Commander Wu Quanmei led them back to Guangdong; several thousand infantry were judiciously reduced.
紅單船 are red-receipt junks, not foreign ships; 提督 is a provincial military commander.
Yongshan, a third-class bodyguard, likewise died fighting Japan at Fengcheng: each has his own biography.
Yongshan, a third-class bodyguard, likewise died fighting Japan at Fenghuangcheng: each has his own biography.
鳳皇城 is Fenghuangcheng; Fengcheng is a different city.
Yongshan, a third-class bodyguard, also at Fengcheng resisted Japan and died fighting strenuously: each has his own biography.
Yongshan, a third-class bodyguard, also at Fenghuangcheng resisted Japan and died fighting strenuously: each has his own biography.
鳳皇城 is Fenghuangcheng; Fengcheng is a different city.
Shubao, whose style was Futing, belonged to the Shumulu clan and served as a Manchu bannerman of the Plain Yellow Banner.
Shubao, whose style was Futing, belonged to the Shumulu clan and was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
滿洲正黃旗人 is banner identity, not an office.
In ten days he fought twenty-eight engagements; Hu Linyi praised his cavalry above all and he received the title Woshihonge Batuer.
In ten days he fought twenty-eight engagements; Hu Linyi praised his cavalry above all and he received the title Woshihong'e Baturu.
倭什洪額巴圖魯 is Woshihong'e Baturu.
Within ten days there were twenty-eight battles large and small; Hu Linyi memorialized that Shubao's cavalry strength had been especially great; he was granted the epithet Woshihonge Batuer.
Within ten days there were twenty-eight battles large and small; Hu Linyi memorialized that Shubao's cavalry strength had been especially great; he was granted the epithet Woshihong'e Baturu.
倭什洪額巴圖魯 is Woshihong'e Baturu.

Taiping and Nian rebels split into two columns and raided Hubei; Brigadier Mu Zhengchun hit the western column and Shubao the eastern, routing them at Huangpi, Guangji, and Yingshan; when the rebels fled back into Henan he was awarded a yellow riding jacket.

Taiping and Nian rebels split into two columns and raided Hubei; Regional Commander Mu Zhengchun hit the western column and Shubao the eastern, routing them at Huangpi, Guangji, and Yingshan; when the rebels fled back into Henan he was awarded a yellow riding jacket.
總兵 is a regional commander, not a brigadier.

Cantonese and Nian bandits split into two routes and fled into Hubei; brigade general Mu Zhengchun struck their western route and Shubao their eastern route, repeatedly defeating them at Huangpi, Guangji, and Yingshan; the bandits fled back into Henan territory; he was granted a yellow riding jacket.

Taiping and Nian bandits split into two routes and fled into Hubei; regional commander Mu Zhengchun struck their western route and Shubao their eastern route, repeatedly defeating them at Huangpi, Guangji, and Yingshan; the bandits fled back into Henan territory; he was granted a yellow riding jacket.
總兵 is a regional commander, not a brigade general; 粵匪 are the Taiping rebels, not Cantonese people.

Linyi halted at Huangzhou, increased Shubao's army by one thousand men, used newly recruited Xidan nomads to roam at Qishui and Shangbahe, and ordered him to lead his old troops to Taihu as a supporting force for Dolonga.

Linyi halted at Huangzhou, increased Shubao's army by one thousand men, used newly recruited Xidan to roam at Qishui and Shangbahe, and ordered him to lead his old troops to Taihu as a supporting force for Dolonga.
西丹 are new Manchu recruits; 游牧 here means they were sent to patrol, not that they were nomads.
In the third year of Xianfeng (1853) he volunteered for active service and was sent from the Yangzhou headquarters.
In the third year of Xianfeng (1853) he volunteered for active service and was sent to the Yangzhou headquarters.
發揚州大營 means he was dispatched to the Yangzhou headquarters, not from it.
In the third year of Xianfeng he volunteered for military service and was dispatched from the Grand Camp at Yangzhou.
In the third year of Xianfeng he volunteered for military service and was dispatched to the Grand Camp at Yangzhou.
發揚州大營 means dispatched to the Yangzhou grand camp, not from it.

Yixing'e took several hundred picked troops, stormed the rebel stronghold, and captured Wang and Liang; when reinforcements came he beat them back, was noted for vice commandant-general, and received the peacock feather.

Yixing'e took several hundred picked troops, stormed the rebel stronghold, and captured Wang and Liang; when reinforcements came he beat them back, was entered on the list for vice commandant-general, and received the peacock feather.
以副都統記名 means entered on the list for that appointment, not merely noted.

In the third year he fought Nian rebels west of De'an and pursued them to Shoushan; at dusk, on broken ridges and in deep ravines ill suited to cavalry, the enemy swelled around him; trapped in heavy encirclement, Shubao cleared a ridge, was thrown from his horse, and died fighting; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted hereditary Master Commandant of Cavalry and Junior Cloud Commandant, enshrined in the Temple of Loyal Loyalty, given a private shrine in Hubei, and honored with the posthumous name Zhenke.

In the third year he fought Nian rebels west of De'an and pursued them to Shoushan; at dusk, on broken ridges and in deep ravines ill suited to cavalry, the enemy swelled around him; trapped in heavy encirclement, Shubao fell from his horse crossing a ditch, and died fighting; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted hereditary Cavalry Commandant and Cloud-Cavalry Commandant, enshrined in the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, given a private shrine in Hubei, and honored with the posthumous name Zhenke.
越坎 is a ditch, not a ridge; 騎都尉 and 雲騎尉 are Cavalry Commandant and Cloud-Cavalry Commandant; 昭忠祠 is the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, not 'Loyal Loyalty'.

In the third year he attacked Nian bandits west of De'an and pursued to Shoushan; at dusk, amid layered hills and deep ravines unfavorable to cavalry combat, the bandits came in ever greater numbers; Shubao fell into heavy encirclement, crossed a ridge and fell from his horse, exhausted his strength and died on the field; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted the hereditary offices of Master Commandant of Cavalry and Junior Cloud Commandant, entered the worship at the Temple of Loyalty and Fidelity, a special shrine was built in Hubei, posthumous title Zhenke.

In the third year he attacked Nian bandits west of De'an and pursued to Shoushan; at dusk, amid layered hills and deep ravines unfavorable to cavalry combat, the bandits came in ever greater numbers; Shubao fell into heavy encirclement, fell from his horse crossing a ditch, exhausted his strength and died on the field; he was posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted the hereditary offices of Cavalry Commandant and Cloud-Cavalry Commandant, entered the worship at the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty, a special shrine was built in Hubei, posthumous title Zhenke.
坎 is a ditch, not a ridge; the two hereditary offices are not 'Master' and 'Junior' grades; 昭忠祠 is the Shrine of Manifest Loyalty.
He served in the Kashgar campaign, was made a vanguard commandant, and was selected for appointment as a bodyguard.
He served in the Kashgar campaign, was made a lieutenant of valiant cavalry, and was selected for appointment as a bodyguard.
驍騎校 is a lieutenant, not a vanguard commandant.
He followed the campaign against Kashgar, was appointed a vanguard commandant, and was selected and appointed a bodyguard.
He followed the campaign against Kashgar, was appointed a lieutenant of valiant cavalry, and was selected and appointed a bodyguard.
驍騎校 is a lieutenant, not a vanguard commandant.
Qi Shan ordered him to reinforce Jiangpu; he first feigned weakness, then struck the rebel camp, routed them at Liushuba, took Jiufuzhou, and was promoted to first-class bodyguard.
Qishan ordered him to reinforce Jiangpu; he first feigned weakness, then struck the rebel camp, routed them at Liushuba, took Jiufuzhou, and was promoted to first-class bodyguard.
琦善 is Qishan, not a surname Qi plus Shan.

Qi Shan ordered him to reinforce Jiangpu; when he first arrived he feigned weakness and did not fight, then stormed the bandit camp and greatly defeated them at Liushuba, broke Jiufuzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to first-class bodyguard.

Qishan ordered him to reinforce Jiangpu; when he first arrived he feigned weakness and did not fight, then stormed the bandit camp and greatly defeated them at Liushuba, broke Jiufuzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to first-class bodyguard.
琦善 is Qishan, not a surname Qi plus Shan.
He posted detachments to guard Xuzhou and Suzhou; when Zhang Luoxing attacked, he and Brigadier Fu Zhenbang drove him off.
He posted detachments to guard Xuzhou and Suzhou; when Zhang Luoxing attacked, he and Regional Commander Fu Zhenbang drove him off.
總兵 is a regional commander.
He divided his army to guard Xuzhou and Suzhou; when Zhang Luoxing came to invade, together with brigade general Fu Zhenbang he attacked and drove them off.
He divided his army to guard Xuzhou and Suzhou; when Zhang Luoxing came to invade, together with regional commander Fu Zhenbang he attacked and drove them off.
總兵 is a regional commander.
In the seventh year he induced five thousand Nian under Chen Baoyuan at Wangjiaxu to surrender, executed their leader Li Yue, and received the title Etuhun Batuer.
In the seventh year he induced five thousand Nian under Chen Baoyuan at Wangjiaxu to surrender, executed their leader Li Yue, and received the title Etuhun Baturu.
巴圖魯 is Baturu, not Batuer.
In the seventh year he induced the Wangjiaxu Nian partisans under Chen Baoyuan, five thousand men, to surrender, beheaded their chief Li Yue, and was granted the title Etuhun Batuer.
In the seventh year he induced the Wangjiaxu Nian partisans under Chen Baoyuan, five thousand men, to surrender, beheaded their chief Li Yue, and was granted the title Etuhun Baturu.
巴圖魯 is Baturu, not Batuer.

He soon led cavalry against Qiaojiamiao, captured and executed Nian chief Liang Sizhu, struck Fengjiaxu by night and killed rebel chief Liu Dayuan, and with Brigadier Shi Rongchun routed the enemy at Zhaojiatun.

He soon led cavalry against Qiaojiamiao, captured and executed Nian chief Liang Sizhu, struck Fengjiaxu by night and killed rebel chief Liu Dayuan, and with Regional Commander Shi Rongchun routed the enemy at Zhaojiatun.
總兵 is a regional commander, not a brigadier.

Shortly afterward he led cavalry to attack Qiaojiamiao, captured and beheaded Nian chief Liang Sizhu; at night he advanced to attack Fengjiaxu and executed bandit chief Liu Dayuan; together with brigade general Shi Rongchun he broke the bandits at Zhaojiatun.

Shortly afterward he led cavalry to attack Qiaojiamiao, captured and beheaded Nian chief Liang Sizhu; at night he advanced to attack Fengjiaxu and executed bandit chief Liu Dayuan; together with regional commander Shi Rongchun he broke the bandits at Zhaojiatun.
總兵 is a regional commander, not a brigade general.
Brigadier Qiu Lian'en had just been killed at Wuyang, two hundred li from Shangshui; when news of Yixing'e's victory spread, the Wuyang rebels fled.
Regional Commander Qiu Lian'en had just been killed at Wuyang, two hundred li from Shangshui; when news of Yixing'e's victory spread, the Wuyang rebels fled.
總兵 is a regional commander.
At that time brigade general Qiu Lian'en fell in battle at Wuyang; Wuyang was two hundred li from Shangshui; by the time of the victory the Wuyang bandits fled at the news.
At that time regional commander Qiu Lian'en fell in battle at Wuyang; Wuyang was two hundred li from Shangshui; by the time of the victory the Wuyang bandits fled at the news.
總兵 is a regional commander.
His request to reward the officers who fought at Laohupo was referred to Acting Grain Transport Governor Yuan Jiasan for review.
His request to reward the officers who fought at Laohupo was referred to Acting Grain Transport Governor-General Yuan Jiasan for review.
署漕督 is an acting director-general of grain transport, a governor-generalship, not a provincial governorship.
The officers and men he requested rewarded for the victory at Laohupo were referred to Acting Grain Transport Governor Yuan Jiasan for investigation and memorial.
The officers and men he requested rewarded for the victory at Laohupo were referred to Acting Grain Transport Governor-General Yuan Jiasan for investigation and memorial.
署漕督 is an acting governor-general of grain transport.
In the spring of the eleventh year he and Xuzhou Garrison Brigadier Teng Jiasheng led two thousand horse to Dongping and Wenshang and won a series of victories.
In the spring of the eleventh year he and Xuzhou Garrison Regional Commander Teng Jiasheng led two thousand horse to Dongping and Wenshang and won a series of victories.
徐州鎮總兵 is a regional commander.

In the spring of the eleventh year, together with Xuzhou garrison brigade general Teng Jiasheng he led two thousand cavalry in haste; they attacked bandits at Dongping and Wenshang and won repeated victories.

In the spring of the eleventh year, together with Xuzhou garrison regional commander Teng Jiasheng he led two thousand cavalry in haste; they attacked bandits at Dongping and Wenshang and won repeated victories.
總兵 is a regional commander.

An edict restored his original office, granted the hereditary office of Cavalry Commandant, posthumous title Zhuangmin, and shrines were built at Xuzhou, Wenshang, Suzhou, and Yongcheng.

Enlisting as a common soldier, he followed Jiang Zhongyuan against rebels in Hubei and rose to major.

From the ranks he followed Jiang Zhongyuan in suppressing bandits in Hubei and was repeatedly promoted to major.

參將 is an assistant regional commander; 巴圖魯 is Baturu.

Sheng Bao praised his youth and courage; he was specially made regional commander of the northern Sichuan garrison, transferred to Xuzhou, and assigned to assist in regional military affairs.

Sheng Bao recommended his youth and bravery; he was exceptionally appointed brigade general of the northern Sichuan garrison, transferred to the Xuzhou garrison, and assisted in Xu and Su military affairs.

unresolvedReferences.description: The packet title (simplified 都兴阿, a colon after 弟, and the English 'Dou Xinga', 'Xi Ling a', 'Fu Minga', 'Shu Bao', 'Yi Xinge', 'Guan Bao') does not match unit s0002, which is 都興阿弟西凌阿福興富明阿舒保伊興額滕家勝關保, idiomatically 'Du Xing'a, his younger brother Xi Ling'a, Fu Xing, Fuming'a, Shubao, Yixing'e, Teng Jiasheng, and Guanbao'.
The Chinese has ★匪, a censored or missing character before 匪. Both English fields render it only as 'bandits'/'rebels' and do not restore the character.

崇煥裔死 is ambiguous: it may mean one descendant of Chonghuan died, which is how the literal English reads, or a looser statement about his posterity. The idiomatic 'line died out' contradicts 有子文弼 in the same sentence. Wenbi's exact father is not named.
玉《角枼》 is a broken glyph for 玉韘 (a jade archer's thumb-ring). Both English fields say 'jade horn cup'.
The Chinese has two U+200B zero-width spaces between 擾 and 虞 (賊擾\u200b\u200b虞、夏邑、鹿邑). The English reads the place as Yucheng and does not show the marks.
